source_text:
## Acceptance checklist (2026-09-30)

- [x] This mission specifies golden/live dataset identity, lifecycle-event vocabulary, event-versus-projection boundaries, and the Hyperreal Side A replay scenario. (evidence: `holes/missions/M-essays-diachronic-model.md`)
- [ ] A named command or script mints a writable Hyperreal live round from an immutable golden seed without modifying the source pair.
- [ ] XTDB document shapes exist for `dataset-round` and the lifecycle events named in this mission.
- [ ] Save-time transitions emit the applicable lifecycle events with stable essay, section, annotation, and dataset-round identities.
- [ ] A replay distinguishes preserved-anchor, forced-reanchor, and substrate-removal transitions in its projections.
- [ ] Temporal query and WebArxana views expose the lifecycle and identify the live round from which every result was derived.

sentences.unresolved_reason: Heading only; names the checklist and date, carries no interpretable move.
Already-checked item with an evidence pointer; background context, not the tasked checklist item (s3).

fragments.text: A named command or script mints
fragments.target: a named command or script that performs the mint operation
fragments.rationale: The acceptance item requires a deliverable with a stable, invocable name: one entry point that performs the mint, not ad hoc REPL steps. That is the shape of an encapsulated command.

pattern_refs.rationale: The item demands the mint be encapsulated as a named, invocable unit with a defined effect, matching the Command-value shape this pattern prescribes.

pattern_rejections.reason: That pattern is about helper commands inside the pattern-library toolchain; this item asks for a first-class deliverable script in the diachronic-model mission, not a library maintenance helper.
pattern_rejections.query: name a command that performs one well-defined action

fragments.text: a writable Hyperreal live round from an immutable golden seed
fragments.target: the writable live round derived from the immutable golden seed
fragments.rationale: The core move: produce a mutable working layer (the live round) whose basis is a fixed, immutable seed. The seed stays the auditable record while the derived round accepts writes.

pattern_refs.rationale: Same structural split: an immutable declared basis (VISION / golden seed) with a mutable working layer (PLAN / live round) whose changes are traceable back to the locked basis.

pattern_rejections.reason: That pattern governs ongoing bidirectional sync with version logging against an evolving upstream; this item is a one-shot mint of a working copy from a fixed seed, with no sync-back channel.
pattern_rejections.query: derive a mutable working copy from an immutable source without modifying the original

fragments.target: the golden source pair, which must remain untouched
fragments.rationale: A guard condition on the mint: derivation must copy, never mutate. This is what keeps the golden seed immutable and makes later replay against it meaningful.
